narrativeReportMd:
# Location R4-to-R6 breaking-change assessment

## Bottom line
`Location` has several local hard instance-breaking changes. The highest-impact changes are the replacement of direct `telecom` with structured `contact`, the `physicalType` to `form` path change, and the remodel of opening hours and exceptions around the R6 `Availability` datatype.

## Scope
The report covers the base `Location` resource only. Inherited Resource/DomainResource/Element changes are excluded and listed out of scope.

## Main migration themes
Migration is mostly a structural transform rather than a simple version bump: contact points move under `ExtendedContactDetail`, physical form is renamed, opening-hours fields move into `Availability.availableTime`, and exception text moves toward `Availability.notAvailableTime`. R6 also adds optional data that R4 cannot carry without extensions.

## Highest-impact findings
The hard validation breaks are `Location.telecom`, `Location.physicalType`, the old `Location.hoursOfOperation` backbone shape, and `Location.availabilityExceptions`. `Location.type` is not a hard wire break, but its terminology and meaning changed enough to require business-rule review.

## Findings requiring human review
Human review is most important for lossy contact downgrade, schedule exception interpretation, `Location.type` ConceptMap choices, and R6-only virtual/geospatial/characteristic data.

## Backward-compatible design observations
Several changes could have been less disruptive if old elements had been retained as deprecated aliases or if new structures had been introduced only as optional alternatives. The R6 model is more expressive, but raw R4 instances cannot be accepted without transformation.

## Follow-up analysis
A datatype-level review of `Availability`, `ExtendedContactDetail`, and `VirtualServiceDetail`, plus official ConceptMaps for Location terminology and structural transforms, would improve migration confidence.

summary.executiveSummaryMd: `Location` has hard local breaking changes in contact, physical form, and availability modeling. The main migration concerns are raw element removals/renames, the `Availability` datatype remodel, and terminology drift in `Location.type`. The largest uncertainty is the absence of official ConceptMaps and complete terminology expansions for service/location role mappings.
summary.migrationThemesMd: Most affected R4 instances can be migrated, but not by pass-through validation. Implementers should build explicit transforms for `telecom` to `contact.telecom`, `physicalType` to `form`, `hoursOfOperation[*]` to one `Availability.availableTime[*]`, and `availabilityExceptions` to `notAvailableTime.description` where appropriate. R6-to-R4 downgrade needs extensions or lossy omission for `virtualService`, contact purpose/name/address/organization/period, availability periods, geospatial codes, and characteristics.
summary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high for structural differences because they are directly present in the R4 and R6 StructureDefinition snapshots/differentials. Confidence is medium for exact semantic and terminology migration because official diffs, ConceptMaps, narrative rationale, and terminology-server expansions were not available. Inherited base-artifact changes were intentionally excluded.

findings.title: Location.telecom was replaced by structured Location.contact

semanticText.definition: The contact details of communication devices available at the location. This can include phone numbers, fax numbers, mobile numbers, email addresses and web sites.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 stores location communication endpoints directly as repeated `Location.telecom` `ContactPoint` values.

semanticText.short: Official contact details for the location
semanticText.definition: The contact details of communication devices available at the location. This can include addresses, phone numbers, fax numbers, mobile numbers, email addresses and web sites.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 removes `Location.telecom` and uses `Location.contact`, whose `ExtendedContactDetail` datatype can include purpose, name, telecom, address, organization, and period.

facts.note: The R4 element is absent from the R6 Location snapshot and differential.
R6 adds a new repeated element for official contact details.
Only the nested telecom portion maps cleanly to the old R4 field.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The R6 `Location.contact` definition reuses the R4 `Location.telecom` communication-device wording but broadens it to structured contact records. This is a replacement, not an inherited change.

impact.impactRationaleMd: An R4 instance containing `Location.telecom` uses an element that is not present in R6 and will fail strict R6 validation unless transformed. Generated R4 model classes and FHIRPath expressions that read `Location.telecom` also break. Downgrade is lossy because R6 contact purpose, names, addresses, periods, and especially `ExtendedContactDetail.organization` cannot be folded into R4 `ContactPoint` values.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Losing or misplacing official phone, URL, booking, or billing contacts can affect operational routing and patient-facing directory accuracy.

justification.inferredGoal: Represent richer official contact details for a location than a flat list of ContactPoint values can support.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Add optional `Location.contact` but retain deprecated `Location.telecom` for flat contact points.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The R6 goal of representing richer grouped contact details is reasonable, and removing the flat field makes `Location.contact` the single canonical contact surface. A less-breaking base design could preserve old instances, but it would duplicate the same fact on the same resource and risk indefinite divergence between `telecom` and `contact.telecom`, so the breakage is probably justified rather than clearly avoidable.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The best alternative would add `Location.contact` and keep `Location.telecom` as deprecated for one or more releases, with rules that flat contact points map to `contact.telecom`. That preserves most R4 data and client paths, but it does not fully solve grouped contact metadata and would require reconciliation when both old and new elements are populated.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Would preserve common R4 contacts, but creates overlapping contact representations requiring precedence and conflict rules.

evidence.detail: R4 defines `Location.telecom` as 0..* `ContactPoint`.
R6 defines `Location.contact` as 0..* `ExtendedContactDetail` and has no `Location.telecom` element.
ExtendedContactDetail includes purpose, name, telecom, address, organization, and period.

examples.examplesMd: Examples are minimal fragments showing the changed wire paths, not complete operational Location records.

findings.narrativeMd: `Location.telecom` is removed and replaced by `Location.contact`. This is more than a rename because the new element is a structured contact datatype. Flat R4 contact points can usually be wrapped as `contact.telecom`, but R6 contacts can carry purpose, person names, postal addresses, validity periods, and contact-level organization references that R4 has no local place to store.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 JSON with a top-level `telecom` array is old-valid/new-invalid for R6 base validation. R6 JSON with `contact` is not R4-valid without transformation. Strict parsers, generated accessors, search/extraction logic, and FHIRPath expressions must switch from `Location.telecom` to `Location.contact.telecom` and account for grouped contact metadata.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: For upgrade, wrap each R4 `telecom` item in an `ExtendedContactDetail` entry, normally as `Location.contact[i].telecom[0]`; if existing profiles used `ContactPoint.use`, review whether it should remain on the ContactPoint or become `contact.purpose`. For downgrade, preserve only nested `contact.telecom` in R4 `telecom` and move purpose/name/address/organization/period to extensions or sidecar records if needed.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The richer contact model addresses real limitations of flat contact points, but removing the old element forces migration of every instance and client path. A backward-compatible alternative existed in the form of an additive `contact` element plus deprecated `telecom`, but that would require duplicate-use guidance.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Review implementations that used `Location.telecom` for web booking URLs or billing phone numbers; those are likely candidates for R6 contact purpose grouping.

freshReview.narrativeMd: `Location.telecom` is a common, concrete directory contact path in R4, and R6 removes that wire name in favor of richer `Location.contact` entries. R4 instances with phone, email, fax, or URL contact points become invalid without transformation, generated clients lose a familiar property, and down-converting R6 contact purpose/name/address/organization/period content is not lossless. The richer R6 model is useful, but this is a mature resource and the break lands on operationally important contact information.
keyEvidence: R4 StructureDefinition: `Location.telecom` is 0..* `ContactPoint` for contact details of communication devices at the location.
R6 StructureDefinition: `Location.telecom` is absent and `Location.contact` is 0..* `ExtendedContactDetail`.
R6 `ExtendedContactDetail` includes purpose, name, telecom, address, organization, and period.
freshReview.fmmEffect: R4 Location is trial-use/FMM 3, so it is not protected like normative content, but it is mature enough that a common contact field deserves real compatibility weight; R6 metadata marks Location normative/FMM 5, increasing the cost of carrying an avoidable late break forward.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: R4 instances containing `Location.telecom` fail strict R6 validation unless transformed; generated API paths also change and richer R6 contacts create R6-to-R4 loss.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: A less-breaking R6 base design could add `Location.contact` while retaining deprecated `Location.telecom` as a flat shortcut that maps to `contact.telecom`. That would create duplicate contact representations and require conflict rules when both are present, but it would preserve most existing R4 contact data and client paths while still allowing richer contacts.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree with the existing High impact and Partial alternative judgment: the hard break and downgrade loss are real, but I give the deprecated-shortcut alternative enough weight to make this worth revisiting.

findings.title: Location.physicalType was renamed to Location.form

semanticText.definition: Physical form of the location, e.g. building, room, vehicle, road.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 used the `physicalType` element for building, room, vehicle, road, and similar physical-form classifications.

semanticText.definition: Physical form of the location, e.g. building, room, vehicle, road, virtual.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 uses the shorter `form` name and explicitly includes virtual as an example of location form.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The old and new elements share cardinality, type, summary flag, requirements, and near-identical definitions, with a path/name and value set URL change.

impact.impactRationaleMd: An R4 instance containing `physicalType` has an unknown element in R6, and an R6 instance containing `form` has an unknown element in R4. The data can often be transformed losslessly for existing codes, but raw validation and generated property access break.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Physical-form classification affects directory search, capacity, and routing logic but is not usually a direct clinical safety field.

justification.inferredGoal: Use a shorter, broader name that can include virtual forms rather than only physical types.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain `Location.physicalType` with broadened wording and value set, or keep it as a deprecated alias while adding `Location.form`.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Broadening the concept to include virtual forms is reasonable, but the R6 goal did not require removing the R4 path. Under the calibration rules, retaining a nonoptimal old name plus clearer definitions is a serious backward-compatible option, so the rename looks probably avoidable.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: R6 could have kept `physicalType` as the base element and updated its definition and example value set to include non-physical or virtual forms. Alternatively, `form` could have been added while `physicalType` remained as a deprecated alias with a simple equivalence rule. Either design would preserve most R4-valid instances with only moderate naming and cleanup tradeoffs.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: The main cost is living with an outdated element name or temporary alias, which is modest compared with a wire-level rename.

evidence.detail: R4 defines `Location.physicalType` as 0..1 `CodeableConcept`, summary true, example-bound to location-physical-type.
R6 defines `Location.form` as 0..1 `CodeableConcept`, summary true, example-bound to location-form; `Location.physicalType` is absent.
Local evidence shows both value sets include `http://terminology.hl7.org/CodeSystem/location-physical-type`; no full expansion was performed.

examples.examplesMd: The normal upgrade transform is a path rename from `physicalType` to `form`.

findings.narrativeMd: `Location.physicalType` disappears and `Location.form` appears with the same cardinality and type. The change is likely intended to support a broader concept of location form, including virtual locations, but it is still a wire-level rename: old JSON cannot be accepted by R6 without moving the data.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: This is hard instance-breaking in both raw directions because the element name changed. Binding strength is only example, so terminology validation is not the main break; the property path is. Generated classes also change property names, which affects serializers, mappers, and search/index extraction logic.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Move `Location.physicalType` to `Location.form` during upgrade and reverse that mapping during downgrade when the coding is meaningful in R4. If R6 uses a virtual-specific form code not recognized by the R4 value set, preserve it with an extension or accept terminology loss.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: A deprecated alias or retaining the old element with updated wording would have avoided a raw instance break. The tradeoff would be a less precise element name and potential confusion between `physicalType` and virtual form.

freshReview.narrativeMd: `Location.physicalType` to `Location.form` is essentially a wire-name replacement with the same cardinality and datatype. Existing R4 data using `physicalType` becomes invalid in R6 even though the R6 value set still draws from the same `location-physical-type` code system. The R6 wording adds virtual forms, but the compatibility cost of a rename looks disproportionate to that goal.
keyEvidence: R4 StructureDefinition: `Location.physicalType` is 0..1 `CodeableConcept`, summary true, example-bound to `location-physical-type`.
R6 StructureDefinition: `Location.form` is 0..1 `CodeableConcept`, summary true, and `Location.physicalType` is absent.
Local value sets: R4 `location-physical-type` and R6 `location-form` both include `http://terminology.hl7.org/CodeSystem/location-physical-type`.
freshReview.fmmEffect: Trial-use/FMM 3 softens the stability expectation compared with normative content, but this mature path had a simple stable representation and the R6 resource is now normative/FMM 5; a mostly cosmetic rename should carry a high justification burden.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: R4 instances with `Location.physicalType` are rejected by strict R6 validation, and generated code/FHIRPath references to the old property break.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: R6 could have retained `physicalType` with updated wording to include virtual forms, or added `form` while keeping `physicalType` as a deprecated alias for at least a transition. The main tradeoff is living with a less ideal legacy name or duplicate alias metadata, which is modest compared with a wire-level rename.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree with the existing Yes alternative judgment and with treating the change as significant, though the operational safety risk is lower than the overall High label suggests.

findings.title: Location.hoursOfOperation changed from repeated backbone entries to a single Availability datatype

oldState.summary: Repeated Location-specific BackboneElement entries with local child fields.

semanticText.short: What days/times during a week is this location usually open
semanticText.definition: What days/times during a week is this location usually open.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 represents opening hours as repeated `Location.hoursOfOperation` backbone elements, each with `daysOfWeek`, `allDay`, `openingTime`, and `closingTime` children.

newState.summary: A single reusable Availability datatype instance.

semanticText.short: What days/times during a week is this location usually open (including exceptions)
semanticText.definition: What days/times during a week is this location usually open, and any exceptions where the location is not available.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 uses a single `Availability` datatype. Repetitions move inside `hoursOfOperation.availableTime`, with `availableStartTime` and `availableEndTime` replacing the old opening and closing time child names.

facts.note: Outer repetitions are no longer allowed; repeated availability periods live inside the datatype.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The element path is retained, but cardinality and type changed and the old child elements are absent from the R6 Location snapshot. R6 `Availability` carries equivalent and expanded children.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Existing R4 JSON uses an array of backbone objects containing `openingTime` and `closingTime`; R6 expects one `Availability` object with nested `availableTime` entries and different child names. Multiple top-level R4 repetitions also violate the R6 max of 1. Generated backbone classes are replaced by a reusable datatype class.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Incorrect transformation can publish wrong opening hours or hide closure windows, affecting scheduling and patient access.

justification.inferredGoal: Reuse a common availability datatype and support richer availability periods and exceptions.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep the R4 opening-hours backbone and add a separate Availability-based element or deprecated aliases.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Using a reusable `Availability` datatype is a coherent R6 design goal, especially where multiple resources need comparable schedule and exception modeling. A less-breaking design exists, but it would leave two same-resource schedule representations and make canonical interpretation harder, so the level of breakage is probably justified if the goal was a clean shared model.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The best alternative would introduce a new optional Availability-valued element, or retain the old `hoursOfOperation` backbone children as deprecated aliases that map into `Availability.availableTime`. This would preserve R4 instances for common opening-hours cases, but it is incomplete for richer R6 availability periods and would create long-term ambiguity when old and new schedule data disagree.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves R4 schedule instances only by maintaining duplicate schedule models, reconciliation rules, and implementation burden.

evidence.detail: R4 defines `Location.hoursOfOperation` as 0..* `BackboneElement`.
R4 child elements include `daysOfWeek`, `allDay`, `openingTime`, and `closingTime`.
R6 defines `Location.hoursOfOperation` as 0..1 `Availability`.
Availability has repeated `availableTime` entries with days, all-day flag, start time, and end time.

examples.examplesMd: The migration example shows two R4 top-level repetitions becoming two R6 `availableTime` repetitions inside one `Availability` object.

findings.narrativeMd: The `hoursOfOperation` element keeps its path but changes shape. This is especially risky because code that only checks for the path name may miss that the JSON representation is now a datatype object with nested arrays and renamed time fields. Multiple R4 repetitions must be folded into one R6 object.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 instances with `hoursOfOperation` as an array of backbone objects become invalid in R6 because the max is now 1 and old child names are not valid children of `Availability`. R6 instances using `Availability.period`, `notAvailableTime`, or datatype extensions are not cleanly representable in R4 without extensions or loss.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Upgrade transforms should create one `Location.hoursOfOperation` object, append each R4 repetition to `availableTime`, map `openingTime` to `availableStartTime`, map `closingTime` to `availableEndTime`, and preserve `daysOfWeek` and `allDay`. Test multiple intervals per day, all-day availability, omitted times, and profiles that previously sliced or constrained the R4 backbone.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The reusable datatype likely reduces duplication across resources, but an additive compatibility period could have avoided breaking existing instances. A profile-only or extension-based introduction would have been less disruptive but weaker as a standard base-model guarantee.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Check whether any implementation serializes `hoursOfOperation` as a singleton despite max `*`; those systems still need child-name and type migration even if the outer cardinality does not visibly change in their data.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R6 keeps the `hoursOfOperation` name but changes the shape from repeated R4 backbone entries to one `Availability` value with nested `availableTime` entries and different child names. Raw R4 JSON will not validate as R6, and generated model classes change. However, the core R4 opening-hours fields have direct R6 counterparts, and the new datatype gives a reusable place for structured exceptions, so the break appears tied to a substantive modeling improvement rather than a simple rename.
keyEvidence: R4 StructureDefinition: `Location.hoursOfOperation` is 0..* `BackboneElement` with `daysOfWeek`, `allDay`, `openingTime`, and `closingTime`.
R6 StructureDefinition: `Location.hoursOfOperation` is 0..1 `Availability` and includes exceptions in its definition.
R6 `Availability.availableTime` repeats and has `daysOfWeek`, `allDay`, `availableStartTime`, and `availableEndTime`; `Availability.notAvailableTime` represents unavailable periods.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 3/trial-use means compatibility matters for directory scheduling data, but it also leaves room for a proportionate refactor when the new model solves a broader recurring availability problem.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: R4 instances with the old backbone array and child names do not match the R6 `Availability` shape; generated API classes and R6-to-R4 conversion of richer exception data also change.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: A less-breaking design could keep the R4 backbone as deprecated or introduce a separate Availability-valued element while leaving `hoursOfOperation` unchanged. That would preserve old instances, but it would maintain two schedule models, require precedence and reconciliation rules, and make adoption of the reusable `Availability` datatype less clean.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree with the existing High impact and Partial alternative judgment: the break is real, but the alternative carries enough duplicate-model cost that I judge the R6 change probably acceptable.

findings.title: Location.availabilityExceptions was removed and only partially maps to Availability.notAvailableTime

oldState.summary: Single free-text exception description on Location.

semanticText.definition: A description of when the locations opening ours are different to normal, e.g. public holiday availability.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 carried exception text separately from opening-hour repetitions.

newState.summary: No direct Location element; exceptions are part of the Availability datatype.

semanticText.short: Not available during this time due to provided reason
semanticText.definition: The item is not available during this period of time due to the provided reason.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 has no `Location.availabilityExceptions` element. The closest model is `Location.hoursOfOperation.notAvailableTime`, with `description` and optional `during` period inside `Availability`.

facts.note: This path is through the R6 Availability datatype, not a direct Location child in the Location snapshot.

facts.newValue: 0..* notAvailableTime entries with description and optional Period

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The R6 `hoursOfOperation` definition explicitly includes exceptions, and `Availability.notAvailableTime.description` is the closest semantic target. The mapping is inferred from definitions rather than from an official ConceptMap.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Any R4 instance with `availabilityExceptions` contains a removed element and will fail R6 validation without transformation. The likely R6 target is richer and repeatable, so R6 exception periods cannot downgrade to the single R4 string without losing structure.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Exception text often communicates public-holiday closures, seasonal schedules, or maintenance downtime; losing it can mislead scheduling and directory users.

justification.inferredGoal: Fold schedule exceptions into the reusable Availability model instead of keeping a Location-specific free-text field.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain deprecated `availabilityExceptions` as a free-text shortcut while adding structured `notAvailableTime` entries.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Moving exception information into `Availability.notAvailableTime` is a reasonable cleanup because exceptions are part of availability, not a separate Location-level concern. Keeping the R4 string would reduce breakage, but it would duplicate closure semantics and create conflict risk with structured periods, so the breaking consolidation is probably justified.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking base design could have kept `Location.availabilityExceptions` as deprecated text and recommended migration to `hoursOfOperation.notAvailableTime.description`. That covers existing R4 data, but it only handles unstructured exceptions and would require rules for how the deprecated text interacts with multiple R6 `notAvailableTime` entries.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Would preserve old exception text, but leaves two places for closure information and weakens adoption of structured periods.

evidence.detail: R4 defines `Location.availabilityExceptions` as 0..1 `string`.
R6 Location has no `Location.availabilityExceptions` element; `Location.hoursOfOperation` says it includes exceptions.
R6 Availability provides `notAvailableTime.description` and `notAvailableTime.during` for unavailable periods and reasons.

examples.examplesMd: A free-text R4 exception can be carried as a R6 `notAvailableTime.description`, but date-specific R6 periods have no R4 core target.

findings.narrativeMd: The R4 free-text exception field is removed. R6 appears to expect exceptions to be part of `Availability.notAvailableTime`, which is better structured but not a direct one-to-one element path. This can be missed if migration only handles normal opening hours.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 data with `availabilityExceptions` is old-valid/new-invalid until moved. R6 data with multiple `notAvailableTime` entries or `during` periods can be downgraded only by concatenating text or using extensions, so round-trip fidelity is limited.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Upgrade by creating or reusing `Location.hoursOfOperation` and adding a `notAvailableTime` entry whose `description` contains the R4 text. Do not invent `during` periods unless source data supports them. Downgrade should preserve R6 descriptions in `availabilityExceptions` only when a single textual summary is acceptable; otherwise use extensions or manual review.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The structured model is likely better for computable closures, but a deprecated text field could have preserved old instances and let systems gradually adopt periods. The compatibility alternative mainly trades model cleanliness for data continuity.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R4's single free-text `availabilityExceptions` element is removed and the exception concept moves into structured `Availability.notAvailableTime` content under R6 `hoursOfOperation`. Old instances with the text field need transformation, but the R6 model can preserve the text as a description and can add dates or periods that R4 could not carry. The compatibility burden is real, yet it is paired with a clearer model for closures and exceptional availability.
keyEvidence: R4 StructureDefinition: `Location.availabilityExceptions` is 0..1 `string` describing departures from normal opening hours.
R6 StructureDefinition: `Location.availabilityExceptions` is absent and `Location.hoursOfOperation` is defined as including exceptions.
R6 `Availability.notAvailableTime.description` is a 0..1 string and `notAvailableTime.during` is a 0..1 `Period`.
freshReview.fmmEffect: At FMM 3/trial-use, removing a scheduling text field should not be dismissed, but the maturity level still permits a proportionate move from unstructured text into a reusable structured availability datatype.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: R4 instances containing `availabilityExceptions` use a removed top-level element; R6-to-R4 conversion of multiple dated exception periods can be lossy.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: R6 could have retained deprecated `availabilityExceptions` as a free-text shortcut mapped to `hoursOfOperation.notAvailableTime.description`. That would preserve old text, but it would leave closure information in two places and weaken the move to structured unavailable periods.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree with the existing Medium impact and Partial alternative judgment: the old field removal is a genuine break, but the structured replacement makes the less-breaking alternative less attractive.

findings.title: Location.type changed meaning and value set from location role/function to service type

oldState.summary: Function or role type of the location.

binding.description: Indicates the type of function performed at the location.

semanticText.definition: Indicates the type of function performed at the location.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 ties `Location.type` to the location's function/role, using an extensible binding to HL7 v3 ServiceDeliveryLocationRoleType.

newState.summary: Types of services available at the location.

binding.description: Indicates the type of services that are available at this location.

semanticText.short: Types of services available at this location
semanticText.definition: Indicates the type of services that are available at this location.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 keeps the same path but redefines the element around available service types and weakens the binding to preferred.

facts.note: This is a weakening, not a stricter validation requirement.

facts.oldValue: Indicates the type of function performed at the location.
facts.newValue: Indicates the type of services that are available at this location.

facts.note: No local ConceptMap or expansion evidence showed overlap.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Because the R6 binding is preferred, an R4 code is not automatically invalid merely because it is outside the preferred value set. The risk is semantic and operational: systems that used `Location.type` as a location role/function code may silently misinterpret it as a service-type list, and enum generators or validation policies that materialize value sets will change code sets.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Location categorization often drives directory search, referrals, routing, and eligibility logic. Silent terminology drift can return the wrong locations or services.

justification.inferredGoal: Clarify `Location.type` as services available rather than the physical or organizational role of the place.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep `Location.type` as role/function and add a distinct service-type element for services available at the location.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The goal of modeling available services is reasonable, but changing the meaning and preferred terminology of the existing `Location.type` path risks semantic breakage for R4 data and consumers. A distinct service-type element would meet the R6 goal while preserving the old role/function semantics with only moderate model-surface cost, so the break appears probably avoidable.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The less-breaking base design would keep R4 `Location.type` for location role or function, retain or deprecate its old terminology, and add an explicit service classification element for the new service-type value set. This would make migration intent visible instead of overloading a familiar path with changed meaning.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Adds another classification field, but avoids silent semantic repurposing of an existing path.

evidence.detail: R4 binding is extensible to v3-ServiceDeliveryLocationRoleType and the definition is function performed at the location.
R6 binding is preferred to service-type and the definition is services available at the location.
Local value set compose definitions reference different terminology systems/families and no ConceptMap was available.

examples.examplesMd: The examples illustrate the terminology-family shift. Exact code validity depends on terminology expansion and local policy.

findings.narrativeMd: `Location.type` did not move, so this is easy to overlook. Its meaning changed from a role/function classification to services available at the location, and the binding moved from an extensible v3 location-role value set to a preferred service-type value set. This is a semantic compatibility risk more than a base-schema rejection risk.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Base R6 validation should not reject all old R4 codes solely because the binding is now preferred, but stricter profiles, enum-based code generation, analytics, and business rules may break or silently change behavior. R6 service-type codes are not reliably representable as R4 location-role codes without an official map.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Inventory existing `Location.type` code systems and downstream use. Do not blindly copy all R4 `type` codings as R6 service types unless their meaning is service availability. Use an official ConceptMap if one becomes available; otherwise document local mapping decisions and preserve unmapped codings as translations or extensions where necessary.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: A new path for service types would have made the semantic shift explicit and avoided overloading old `type` consumers. The chosen design keeps the familiar path but requires migration review to prevent silent interpretation errors.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: This finding has high structural confidence but only medium terminology-mapping confidence because no expansion or ConceptMap was available.

freshReview.narrativeMd: `Location.type` remains structurally valid as repeating `CodeableConcept`, but its meaning changes from the function performed at the location to services available at the location, and its terminology changes from an extensible v3 role-type value set to a preferred service-type value set. This is a silent semantic break: existing data can pass validation while downstream directory, routing, referral, or eligibility logic reads the same path with a different interpretation.
keyEvidence: R4 StructureDefinition: `Location.type` means type of function performed at the location and is extensible-bound to `v3-ServiceDeliveryLocationRoleType`.
R6 StructureDefinition: `Location.type` means types of services available at this location and is preferred-bound to `service-type`.
Local value sets use different terminology families: v3 RoleCode for R4 and `http://terminology.hl7.org/CodeSystem/service-type` for R6.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 3/trial-use does not prohibit semantic evolution, but this is a mature, summary directory classification field; the risk is not just churn but silent misclassification on a path implementers already know.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: semantic/documentation: old data is usually still syntactically valid, but the same path now carries a different business meaning and validation/code-generation policies may materialize a different code set.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: A clearer less-breaking design would keep `Location.type` for role or function, possibly deprecated, and add a distinct service-type element for available services. That adds another classification field, but it avoids repurposing an existing path and makes migration intent explicit.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree with the existing Medium impact and Yes alternative judgment; the absence of a hard validation break does not remove the need to revisit the semantic repurposing.

findings.title: Location.description type changed from string to markdown

semanticText.short: Additional details about the location that could be displayed as further information to identify the location beyond its name
semanticText.definition: Description of the Location, which helps in finding or referencing the place.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 models the description as a primitive `string`.

semanticText.short: Additional details about the location that could be displayed as further information to identify the location beyond its name
semanticText.definition: Description of the Location, which helps in finding or referencing the place.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 changes only the primitive type to `markdown`; the element path, cardinality, summary flag, and definition remain stable.

facts.note: FHIR markdown is serialized as a primitive string.
This reduces but does not eliminate runtime type/codegen risk.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Plain R4 description strings remain representable as R6 markdown in ordinary cases, and the JSON primitive shape is still a string. The practical risk is generated datatype changes, renderer/sanitizer expectations, and downgrade loss of the explicit markdown rendering contract.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: The field is human-facing directory text; rendering errors or unsafe markdown handling can affect display quality and security posture but not core resource identity.

justification.inferredGoal: Allow formatted descriptive text for Location descriptions.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: No less-breaking base alternative is needed because R4 strings remain JSON-string-compatible with R6 markdown.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The goal of allowing formatted descriptive text is reasonable, and the wire representation remains a JSON string. Because ordinary R4 `string` values are preserved as R6 `markdown`, this is better calibrated as a low-risk type widening rather than a breaking base-design issue.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: Retaining `string` would avoid some code-generation differences, but it would not communicate markdown rendering semantics to tooling. Under the calibration rules, the backward-compatible-alternative question is not applicable because the change preserves R4 instances rather than requiring a less-breaking replacement design.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Generated primitive wrappers and rendering or sanitization behavior may change, but this is not a base R4-to-R6 instance break.

evidence.detail: R4 `Location.description` type is `string`.
R6 `Location.description` type is `markdown`.
The R6 markdown datatype is a primitive type derived from string and intended for GitHub Flavored Markdown processing.

examples.examplesMd: R4 can carry the markdown text as a string, but an R4-only consumer may display markdown syntax literally and may not apply markdown sanitization.

findings.narrativeMd: `Location.description` changes primitive type from `string` to `markdown`. This is not a major wire-format break because both serialize as JSON strings and markdown derives from string, but strongly typed SDKs, validation schemas, and UI renderers may change behavior.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Typical R4 strings should remain valid R6 markdown content. R6 markdown can be downgraded to an R4 string textually, but the fact that the content is intended for markdown rendering is not represented in R4. The main compatibility issue is codegen and UI processing, not base instance rejection.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Update generated types and UI rendering/sanitization pipelines for `Location.description`. Treat migrated R4 text as plain markdown-safe text. When downgrading, preserve the raw text and document that rendering intent may be lost.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: Because serialization stays string-like, this is a relatively safe way to add formatting semantics. The less-breaking alternative of retaining `string` would avoid type changes but would not communicate markdown support to tooling.

freshReview.narrativeMd: Changing `Location.description` from `string` to `markdown` does not create a meaningful instance-compatibility issue because both are primitive JSON strings and ordinary R4 description text remains representable. The main effect is tooling and rendering behavior: generated primitive wrappers or display sanitization may change, but the wire content is not invalidated by the type label alone.
keyEvidence: R4 StructureDefinition: `Location.description` is 0..1 `string`.
R6 StructureDefinition: `Location.description` is 0..1 `markdown`.
R6 `markdown` primitive is defined as a string that may contain GitHub Flavored Markdown syntax, and systems are not required to process markdown.
freshReview.fmmEffect: Even with FMM 3/trial-use maturity, the compatibility mechanism is too small to justify concern; maturity does not turn a same-wire-shape primitive clarification into a hard break.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: metadata/tooling: the primitive label and rendering expectations change, but old string-valued JSON remains a string-valued element in R6.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: No less-breaking base design is needed. Keeping `string` would avoid some generated-type churn, but it would also fail to signal markdown rendering semantics; because old instances remain representable, this is not a design problem.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree with the existing Low impact and Not applicable alternative judgment.

findings.title: R6 added Location.virtualService with no R4 core equivalent

oldState.summary: No core Location element for virtual service connection details.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 `Location` has no local element corresponding to reusable virtual meeting or conference connection details.

semanticText.short: Connection details of a virtual service (e.g. conference call)
semanticText.definition: Connection details of a virtual service (e.g. shared conference call facility with dedicated number/details).

newState.narrativeMd: R6 can represent persistent or shared virtual service connection details directly on Location.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Optional additions do not invalidate old R4 instances when upgrading. They do, however, create a significant downgrade gap because R4 has no base element for virtual-service channel type, address choice, additional information, participant limits, or session key.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Dropping virtual connection details can prevent users from accessing virtual or hybrid locations.

justification.inferredGoal: Represent virtual or telecommunication-based locations in the base resource.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Optional R6 addition; R4 instances are preserved, and R4 extensions are downgrade mitigations rather than base-design alternatives.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Adding optional virtual-service details is the least disruptive base R6 mechanism for a new capability and does not invalidate R4 Location instances. The reported risk is primarily R6-to-R4 representability, so scoring an R4 extension strategy as a backward-compatible alternative would confuse mitigation with base-design compatibility.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: No less-breaking R6 base design is needed for the upgrade direction: absence of `virtualService` in R4 data remains acceptable in R6. Cross-version extensions can preserve this content when downgrading to R4, but they are not a less-breaking alternative to the optional R6 base element.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: R6-to-R4 downgrade may need extensions or lose data, but the additive R6 element is not an R4-to-R6 base break.

evidence.detail: R6 defines `Location.virtualService` as 0..* `VirtualServiceDetail`; no R4 element exists.
VirtualServiceDetail contains channel type, address choice, additional info, max participants, and session key.

examples.examplesMd: The example uses an illustrative channel coding; the key point is the R6-only `virtualService` structure.

findings.narrativeMd: `Location.virtualService` is a new optional R6 capability. It is not an R4-to-R6 validation break, but it is a high downgrade-risk field because it can contain operationally important virtual access details with no R4 core target.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Old R4 instances remain valid with respect to this addition. R6 instances using `virtualService` are not R4-valid unless the content is transformed to extensions or external records. Strict R4 parsers will reject the element.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: For R6-to-R4 downgrade, define a cross-version extension strategy or preserve virtual connection details in an associated scheduling/appointment context when appropriate. Avoid silently dropping `sessionKey`, `additionalInfo`, or dial-in addresses if they are needed for access.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The additive design is backward-compatible in the upgrade direction. No base R4-compatible representation exists except extensions, so a fully backward-compatible alternative would have required standardizing such an extension before or alongside the R6 element.

freshReview.narrativeMd: `Location.virtualService` is an optional R6 addition. It does not invalidate any R4 Location when moving forward to R6. A system that must down-convert R6 virtual connection details to pure R4 may lose channel type, address choice, additional info, participant limits, or session key, but that is the normal reverse-direction limitation of adding useful new optional content, not a reason to revisit the R6 base design.
keyEvidence: R6 StructureDefinition: `Location.virtualService` is 0..* `VirtualServiceDetail`; no corresponding R4 Location element exists.
R6 `VirtualServiceDetail` includes channel type, `address[x]`, additional info, max participants, and session key.
R4 StructureDefinition element list has no `Location.virtualService`.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 3/trial-use does not add stability pressure against optional additions. The change improves R6 expressiveness while preserving all R4 instances in the upgrade direction.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: R6-to-R4 loss: R6 instances using the new optional element cannot be represented losslessly in R4 core, but there is no old-valid/new-invalid R4-to-R6 break.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: No less-breaking R6 base alternative is needed for an optional addition. R4 extensions or cross-version mappings can mitigate downgrade loss, but they are not a less-breaking R6 base design.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: disagree with the existing Medium overall concern while agreeing that downgrade loss exists; for fresh R4-to-R6 review this is an additive no-problem change.

findings.title: R6 added Location.code and Location.characteristic classification elements without R4 core targets

oldState.summary: No direct core fields for geospatial/administrative location codes or generic characteristics.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 has identifiers, type, physicalType, address, and extensions, but no direct `code` or `characteristic` fields on Location.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 adds `Location.code` for geospatial or administrative region codes and `Location.characteristic` for attributes such as wheelchair accessibility.

facts.newValue: No direct equivalent; use extensions or external mapping for downgrade.

impact.impactRationaleMd: These optional R6 additions do not affect validation of old R4 instances, but R6 data using them is not representable in R4 core fields. `Location.code` may overlap conceptually with identifiers or address parts, and `Location.characteristic` may overlap with local extensions; neither has a lossless base R4 target.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Characteristics such as accessibility and geospatial/admin codes can affect discovery, routing, and equity-sensitive directory behavior.

justification.inferredGoal: Add first-class support for coded location identity and attributes.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Optional R6 classification additions; R4-to-R6 compatibility is unaffected.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: First-class coded location and characteristic fields are reasonable optional additions for R6 directories and do not reject existing R4 instances. The compatibility issue is that R6-only content has no R4 core target, which is outside the backward-compatible-alternative judgment for R4-to-R6 base breakage.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: Standard extensions can help R4 systems carry these classifications, but that is a cross-version mitigation. Since the R6 fields are optional additions and preserve old instances, there is no applicable less-breaking base R6 design to score.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: R4 round-trip may rely on extensions or local mapping, but that is a downgrade concern rather than a less-breaking R6 base alternative.

evidence.detail: R6 adds `Location.code` 0..* `CodeableConcept`, summary true, for geospatial/admin codes.
R6 adds `Location.characteristic` 0..* `CodeableConcept` for attributes such as wheelchair accessibility.
R4 has no `Location.code` or `Location.characteristic` elements.

examples.examplesMd: R4 can preserve this information only through extensions, local conventions, or lossy mapping to identifiers/address text.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 adds two optional classification surfaces: `code` for coded geospatial or administrative identity and `characteristic` for attributes. They are non-breaking for upgrade but important for downgrade and round-trip planning because R4 has no equivalent core elements.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4-to-R6 validation is unaffected when these fields are absent. R6 instances containing them will fail R4 validation as unknown elements and cannot be round-tripped without an extension or external mapping convention.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: When downgrading, decide whether `code` should become an extension, a local identifier, or be omitted; do not automatically merge it into `Location.identifier` unless the code truly functions as an identifier. Preserve `characteristic` as a standard or local extension if directory behavior depends on it.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: Additive optional fields are the normal backward-compatible way to evolve a resource in the forward direction. Complete cross-version compatibility would require paired R4 extensions and mapping rules, which were not present in the supplied inputs.

freshReview.narrativeMd: `Location.code` and `Location.characteristic` are optional R6 additions for geospatial/administrative codes and attributes such as wheelchair accessibility. They do not make any R4 instance invalid and do not force existing R4 clients to change when upgrading. Pure R4 down-conversion may need extensions or may lose the new classifications, but that is an expected cost of adding optional expressive fields.
keyEvidence: R6 StructureDefinition: `Location.code` is 0..* `CodeableConcept` for geospatial or administrative codes.
R6 StructureDefinition: `Location.characteristic` is 0..* `CodeableConcept` for attributes such as wheelchair accessibility.
R4 StructureDefinition element list has no `Location.code` or `Location.characteristic`.
freshReview.fmmEffect: The artifact's FMM 3/trial-use maturity does not weigh against additive optional fields that preserve R4 instances; any concern is limited to reverse conversion of new R6 content.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: R6-to-R4 loss: R6 instances using these optional additions have no lossless R4 core target, but there is no forward R4-to-R6 validation or API break.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: No less-breaking R6 base alternative is needed. Standard or local R4 extensions can carry similar concepts during downgrade, but those are migration mitigations rather than changes to the R6 base model.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: disagree with the existing Medium overall concern while agreeing that pure R4 round-trip can lose new R6 data; this additive change is not a meaningful compatibility problem.

checkedNoMaterialChange.notesMd: The canonical URL, id, name, kind, type, baseDefinition, derivation, and abstract flag are unchanged. The metadata status changed from draft to active, which is noted as non-breaking.

No local minimum cardinality increases were found. The material `hoursOfOperation` max decrease is covered as a finding; other retained local elements such as identifier, status, operationalStatus, name, alias, description, mode, type, address, position, managingOrganization, partOf, and endpoint keep their cardinalities.

Local reference targets for `Location.managingOrganization` to Organization, `Location.partOf` to Location, and `Location.endpoint` to Endpoint are unchanged. New nested references inside ExtendedContactDetail are datatype-level details covered in the contact finding.

`Location.status` and `Location.mode` remain required bindings with the same local code sets (`active`, `suspended`, `inactive`; `instance`, `kind`). `Location.operationalStatus` remains preferred-bound to v2-0116. The material `Location.type` binding change is covered separately.
No local Location differential constraints were added, removed, or changed. Snapshot constraint rewrites inherited from base artifacts are out of scope.
No local fixed values, pattern values, default values, maxLength changes, regex constraints, or min/max value limits were found on Location-specific differential elements.
`Location.status` remains the only local modifier element among the examined Location-specific elements. R6 explicit `isModifier: false` values on many elements do not materially change behavior.
No local slicing changes were found in the base Location StructureDefinition.

No resource-level serialization format change was found. Serialization/codegen breaks are limited to local element path/type changes covered in findings, especially contact, form, availability, virtualService, and markdown description.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: StructureDefinition status changed from draft to active
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The artifact identity and wire format are unchanged by metadata status alone.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Governance and conformance tooling may treat an active ballot artifact differently from a draft R4 artifact, but this is not an instance validation break by itself.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: Root definition broadened from physical place to place
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The root resource identity and cardinality are unchanged. The wording aligns with virtual-location support rather than invalidating old physical locations.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Directory and UI logic should not assume every R6 Location is purely physical, especially in combination with `form` and `virtualService`.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: Position comment now points to a boundary GeoJSON extension
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The longitude, latitude, and altitude child cardinalities and types are unchanged; the new text is guidance for representing boundary shapes.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Systems needing areas or polygons should evaluate the referenced boundary extension, but point-coordinate data remains structurally stable.

followUpDependencies.reasonMd: `Location.hoursOfOperation` now depends on R6 `Availability`; a datatype-level report should assess its own cross-version risks and reusable migration strategy.
`Location.contact` uses `ExtendedContactDetail`; downgrade handling depends on nested fields such as purpose, name, address, organization, and period.
`Location.virtualService` introduces a complex R6-only datatype whose address choice and security/session fields need datatype-level migration review.
The most important semantic uncertainty is how, or whether, R4 location role/function codes should map to R6 service-type codes.
Inherited constraint, language-binding, extension, modifierExtension, and primitive datatype changes were intentionally excluded and should be handled by the assigned base-artifact reports.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: No official R4-to-R6 diff, ballot change proposal, or Jira rationale was used. The assessment is based on local package artifacts and inferred migration intent.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Review official HL7 change notes, Jira tickets, and generated diff pages for Location.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: Terminology comparison used local ValueSet/CodeSystem compose evidence, not live terminology-server expansions. External THO systems such as service-type and v3 RoleCode were not fully expanded.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Run version-pinned expansions and compare code overlap, retired codes, displays, and definitions.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: No official ConceptMaps were available for structural or terminology migrations. Mapping guidance is therefore implementer-oriented rather than normative.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Use official cross-version StructureMaps or ConceptMaps if HL7 publishes them for R4-to-R6 Location.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: Inherited changes visible in snapshots, including DomainResource constraints, Resource.language binding, Element/Extension constraints, and modifierExtension summary flags, were excluded by assignment scope.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Consult the separate reports for the base artifacts.
